what: Two independent container readings of Brain's own russell_cycle cursor, at one revision, taken three minutes apart.
whyItExists: L's condition 'its cursor moved between two readings' read FAIL inside each single container run, byte-identical both times. This is what distinguishes a stopped loop from a measurement window narrower than the tick it measures. It is a diagnosis, not a verdict: no code reads this file, and it awards no condition.
conclusion: The deployed loop ticked six times between the two readings. Inside one container run it cannot be seen to move, because the image excludes tests/, docs/ and client/src, so the repository half of the report is skipped and the whole run takes about sixteen seconds against a thirty-second tick. Both readings therefore fall inside one tick. The fix is in the reporter, not the loop: reReadCycle polls for a window two ticks wide. It can still fail, and a loop that has genuinely stopped will still produce the same timestamp for seventy-five seconds.
notAVerdict: L reads FAIL at this revision and stays FAIL. The reporter at dd1f9be evaluated the condition and it did not hold. Nothing here changes that, and no gate consumes this file.
